extracted.intended_audience: researchers and OSF users preparing registrations/preregistrations (including admin contributors, co‑contributors, and registry moderators)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for creating, submitting, updating, and managing OSF registrations and preregistrations (including privacy/embargo, metadata, contributor permissions, updates, withdrawals, and earning Open Practice Badges). Platform-specific instructions for OSF Registry workflows and required fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Registration / Preregistration
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrations are a formal, transparent “story” of your study. This story describes what your research plans to do, any updates that need to be made, and the results. Preregistration is the practice of posting a time-stamped, read-only version of your study plan to a public repository before beginning data collection or analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preregistration establishes a transparent record of research intentions; use it to certify plans in advance of data analysis or to capture the exact state of a project at key lifecycle points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective practices for a rigorous preregistration
rubrics_metrics.description: Be precise and explicit with your plan, make design and analysis decisions before viewing the data, and anticipate contingencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use your preregistration as a way to draft methods/results for a manuscript; list hypotheses and which variables you’ll use; make analysis decisions prior to viewing data; write 'if then' decision trees for contingencies; describe statistical tests and decision criteria; demonstrate methodology and how hypotheses will be tested; state exclusion rules; describe variable combination rules; list model form, covariates, and characteristics; detail reported outcomes; describe planned and potential unplanned analyses; anticipate deviations and include them in your plan. (Source: 'Effective Practices for a Rigorous Preregistration' section; example: 'if the assumptions for this test are violated, we will use this alternate test').

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose the registration template that fits your study
rubrics_metrics.description: Select a registration template appropriate to your study design, community standards, and institutional policies; OSF does not recommend a single template for all studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Available templates include OSF Preregistration (general), Open-Ended, EEG/ERP Methods, Generalized Systematic Review, Social Psychology preregistration, AsPredicted (8 questions), Qualitative Preregistration, Registered Report Protocol (after in-principle acceptance), replication recipes, and Secondary Data Preregistration. Use templates/examples and linked DOIs to decide which fits your project.

rubrics_metrics.name: File size limit for registrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrations archive and preserve both OSF Storage and add-ons connected to projects up to a total of 5GB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you need to create a registration larger than 5GB, contact OSF support. When registering from a project, any files associated with that project (OSF Storage or add-ons) up to 5GB will be included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymization for blinded peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: If submitting for blinded peer-review, ensure no identifying information is included in metadata or attached documents and place the registration under embargo or make it private/anonymized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can create an anonymized view-only link that removes author names on the Registration Overview and the 'Authors' section; ensure attached files are also anonymized. Note: to keep identity hidden in peer review, use embargo and the anonymized view-only link features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registrations are read-only after submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Once you submit a registration, you will not be able to edit or make changes to it or any associated files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents uploaded to or submitted with a registration cannot be modified after submission. To change content you must submit an update (subject to update rules) or, if necessary, withdraw and create a new registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy settings and embargo rules
rubrics_metrics.description: After submission you may make a registration public immediately or place it under embargo (private) for up to four years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select 'Make registration public immediately' to receive a DOI (DOIs are only available for public registrations). For embargo: choose an embargo end date (format YYYY-MM-DD). Embargo can be up to 4 years from creation. Once a registration is made public it cannot be embargoed again; to make it effectively private you'd need to withdraw and submit a new embargoed registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval and auto-approval workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: When a registration is submitted, all admin contributors are notified and can approve or cancel the submission; after 48 hours the submission is automatically approved unless submitted to a Community-run Registry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The registration shows 'Pending Approval' during this period. If any admin rejects the registration within 48 hours the submission is cancelled and returned to draft; if admins do nothing it auto-approves after 48 hours. Community-run registries may have different moderation/approval workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archiving restrictions during submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not add, edit, or delete any files or contents during the archiving process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modifying files during archiving causes archiving failure and will require creating a new registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration metadata fields and discoverability
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide complete metadata to help others discover, cite, and evaluate studies: Title, Description, Contributors, Licenses, Institutional Affiliations, Subjects, Tags, Resource Type, Language, Funding/Support, Publication DOI, and more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metadata is editable from the registration page (except some items like the Registration DOI). Resource type and language use DataCite schema dropdowns. Funding/support should use Crossref Funder Registry entries where possible to include funder IDs; add award titles, URIs, and award numbers as relevant. Subjects help classification; tags help searchability—start with broad then specific terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contributor roles, bibliographic status, and permissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Contributors must be added with specific permissions; co-authors are given read+write by default; permission levels can be bibliographic or non-bibliographic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permission levels described: Read — can view the registration but not edit; Read + Write — can view and (page text inconsistent: states 'does not have permission to edit' but also 'author can add supplemental files') — intended to allow collaborators to edit drafts before submission; Administrator — can view/edit the registration, add supplemental files, manage authors and permissions, start updates, and submit requests to end embargos early. Non-bibliographic contributors keep permissions but are not listed as authors. If adding contributors, assign appropriate permissions and use 'Add Contributor by Search' or 'Add Unregistered Contributor' (enter name and email). Reordering authors sets citation order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Saving and draft management
rubrics_metrics.description: Draft registrations are autosaved; you can access drafts from 'My Registrations' and delete drafts irreversibly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Autosave occurs when moving between sections; an email with a link to the draft is sent when creating a draft—save that link. Deleting a draft is IRREVERSIBLE and cannot be recovered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Updates: when allowed and required justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Updates are for transparently reflecting necessary changes (events outside your control or unexpected anomalies) and require a required justification text box explaining why the update is needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only admin collaborators can start an update. Update drafts prepopulate previous responses; you must change at least one field to submit an update. Files cannot be added or removed during an update. Contributors should enter justification as they make edits. Upon submission of an update, admins have 48 hours to approve/reject; updates auto-approve after 48 hours unless on a Community-run Registry.

rubrics_metrics.name: View-Only Links (VOL) and anonymized VOL
rubrics_metrics.description: You can create view-only links for public or embargoed registrations; links can be anonymized to mask contributor names and activity—useful for blinded peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only admins can create VOLs (not visible to read or read+write users). To create: open registration -> Contributors tab -> Create -> name the link, choose anonymization, and create. Copyable via clipboard icon. Removing the VOL prevents further access for that link; removal confirmed via delete modal.

rubrics_metrics.name: End embargo early workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: Admin contributors may request to end an embargo early; the request must be approved by all admins and auto-approves after 48 hours if no response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the embargoed registration tab select 'End Embargo Early', confirm, and submit the request; admins receive notification and can approve or cancel via email; after 48 hours it auto-approves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdraw a registration — irreversible and preserves tombstone metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: Withdrawing removes registration content from OSF but preserves basic metadata (title, contributors, DOI, dates) and a justification; withdrawal is irreversible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If registration is embargoed you must end embargo to withdraw. To withdraw: open registration -> Public registration tab -> 'Withdraw registration' -> enter justification -> submit. Registration shows 'Pending withdrawal' and admins must approve via email; if no action taken it auto-withdraws after 48 hours. After withdrawal the Registration Overview remains with a withdrawal note and the justification (displayed). On original project's 'Registrations' page the registration is marked 'Withdrawn'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forced withdrawal by moderators on branded registries
rubrics_metrics.description: Moderators on Community-run (branded) registries may forcibly withdraw registrations that violate registry policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contributors will be notified by email of forced withdrawal and its reasoning. Branded registries may also moderate submissions pre-approval to enforce custom standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Practice Badges — general requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Open Practice Badges are awarded when a researcher links a resource to their registration and meets that badge’s specified criteria; researchers are responsible for adhering to criteria and for legal authority to assert resource compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To earn a badge the resource must be stored in an open-access repository with a DOI, be time-stamped/immutable/permanent where required, and meet the badge-specific criteria. Displaying a badge on your registration means all contributors have permission and legal authority for the resource.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Data badge criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Awarded when digitally shareable data necessary to reproduce reported results are publicly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data must be publicly available on an open-access repository with a DOI (time-stamped, immutable, permanent), include a data dictionary with enough information to reproduce results, and have an open license allowing copying, distribution, and use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Analytic Code badge criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Awarded when analytical code needed to reproduce reported analyses is publicly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Code must be publicly available on an open-access repository with a DOI, include information so a researcher knows how the code plays into the study design, and use an open license allowing reuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Materials badge criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Awarded when components of the research methodology needed to reproduce procedures and analysis are publicly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materials must be publicly available on an open-access repository with a DOI; any components that cannot be digitally shared should be described with enough information to reproduce them; include information about how materials relate to the study design and assign an open license.

rubrics_metrics.name: Papers badge criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Awarded when manuscripts, papers, reports, and articles generated from the study are publicly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers must be publicly available on an open-access repository with a DOI. Examples include peer-reviewed articles, book chapters, dissertations, manuscripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplements badge criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Awarded when other resources related to a study not covered by other badges are publicly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplements must be publicly available on an open-access repository with a DOI. Examples: data management plans, data dictionaries, events, figures, IRB documents, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add resource to registration: process and immutable archived links
rubrics_metrics.description: To add a resource (Data, Code, Materials, Papers, Supplements) provide DOI, resource type, and description; archived links from projects/registrations cannot be modified later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From Registration Overview or Resources tab, select resource icon -> Add Resource -> enter DOI, resource type, description -> Preview -> Add. Linked project/registration links included on a registration are immutable and changes to original project links are not reflected on the archived registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource metadata & funding information requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Resource information (type, language) uses DataCite choices; funding/support should use Crossref Funder Registry entries where possible and include award title, URI, and award number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select resource type and language from dropdowns (DataCite schema); add funder via registry lookup to include funder ID; multiple funders can be added; save changes to record them. Registration DOI is shown but not editable.

rubrics_metrics.name: If a required field is not relevant, provide an explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: When a required registration field does not apply to your study, provide an explanation as to why the field does not pertain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration fields are intended to produce a complete picture of the study; if something truly does not apply, include a short justification explaining irrelevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document and update limitations: no uploads/changes after submission and during updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents cannot be uploaded to a registration after it is submitted or to any update; documents submitted with a registration cannot be modified once registered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To include additional files after submission, link files from a public project, newly submitted public registration, or any external repository via a DOI. During an update you cannot add or remove files—only edit prepopulated text fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: What to include for archiving: provide detailed plan and supporting documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrations are best served by providing as detailed a plan as possible for archiving—the registration should tell the complete 'story' with supporting documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare documentation that describes methods, planned analyses, outcomes, exclusion rules, data/code/materials locations (with DOIs), and any other information necessary for archiving and reproducibility.
